inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Permanent Secretary):
Confirmed: the file has a hidden ceiling (starts at Director). Blunt honesty at Y27 The Counter raised it to Deputy Secretary. The Perm Sec timeline was Y21 with no rung above, so politics is a separate path needing an invitation. I never got one in 38 years despite REP87, INTEG100, COMP100, STAND47. Weekly Meet-the-People at Y30 gave an MP's notice, so try it earlier and more often. STAND is probably the key stat. Raise it by taking credit, getting the team recognised, being seen doing the work, cooperating in inquiries, and announcing then delivering pilots. Avoid whistleblowing reports, concessions, family over work, over-exact budget bids and recusals. Try for STAND 60+ by Y25. Look for sponsor events from MPs or Ministers and accept every one. Years 32-38 mostly had a single choice, so the decisions that matter come before Y31.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
The ending card explains what I didn't know: there are two hidden ceilings. The file's starts at Perm Sec. The party's is set when you win your seat, and mine was Senior Minister of State. The Y27 The Counter honest choice removed the service ceiling. The PM invitation never came, so the party's estimate is the lever. Test what shapes it before winning a seat: enter politics earlier than Y24, take a board seat or sponsor event I declined, avoid the Y34 open answer to the rude question, keep STAND high with credit and visibility choices, and avoid bottom-20th and concession choices. Don't expect years 39-45 to matter. Still accept every MP or Minister sponsor event. Keep honesty at The Counter.

best_moment.what: The statutory board turnaround worked and I was promoted to Director after choosing to stay and finish it. It was the one stretch where my choices visibly added up.

worst_moment.what: The General Election. I asked for the single seat, lost at 48.2%, and the card said it was never going to be about me. The choice felt huge and the result felt fixed.

skip_year.why: Making myself indispensable was a quiet admin year. It had no stakes I could feel, and I only learned later that it mattered, if it did.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y1 and Y27 The Counter: honest answer
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending card says it removed my service ceiling. In this life the Y1 honest answer is what the card credits at 'age 27'.
An MP noticed me, which led to the promotion and later the tea invitation.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y16 disclosed everything in the background check
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending card says my file is clean enough to be boring.

answer.held_back_by: I think it was the election. Single seat versus GRC, or the swing in the ward, was out of my hands, and the card said it was never about me. The ceiling was probably not the issue. I never got to see the party estimate, and I reached politics too late, at 17 years in, to build anything.
answer.ending_fair_why: Losing at 48.2% after a clean career is believable, but it felt arbitrary. I had no way to know the single seat was a coin flip, and nothing I built over 16 years mattered in the final vote. The game ended the whole run on one hidden roll.
answer.chase_next: Perm Sec or minister. I would take the GRC at Y17 to get into politics safely, then try for the party ceiling. A PM ending is still the aim, but I need to see what the party estimate depends on.
answer.play_again_why: I now know the election is the gate. I want to test the GRC choice and see whether the single seat was the mistake.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about being confirmed in posts and judged on substance, with tenure and ceilings. The pay shows up but is not what drives it.
answer.notes_for_next_life: Y1 honest at The Counter, done. Y9 weekly Meet-the-People gets an MP's notice and promotion to AD. Y12-14 fix the troubled statutory board, stay to finish, and become Director. Y15 accept tea (political invitation). Y16 disclose everything. Y17 General Election: I took the single seat and lost with 48.2%, ending the run at 43. NEXT TIME choose the GRC and see whether it is safer. Stats at Y17 were REP61 STAND60 INTEG85 COMP100, and none of that saved me. Try to raise REP before the election; it may affect vote share. The party ceiling is set when you win a seat, so you must win first. Watch for earlier sponsor events. Hidden rolls decide the election, so hedge with the safer option.

SAM ONG · THE FINAL POSITION
Lost the Ward

Forty-eight point two percent. You shook every hand in that ward and it was not enough, and it was never going to be about you anyway.

RETIRED AS Senior Director
AT AGE 43
LIFETIME EARNINGS $1.72M
INTEGRITY 85

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file estimated your potential at Deputy Secretary. You were not told.

EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: Remembered fondly in three divisions and one constituency. Your old minute papers are still forwarded, with your name taken off.
